title: What SCIM does when a user is disabled or deleted

prose.text: "We disabled the user in the IdP, why can they still browse?" starts with which SCIM action the IdP really sends. {{active-flag}} {{delete-removes}} {{idp-deactivation-actions}} Which request an IdP sends when a user is deleted from the directory is open {{gap:deletion-request}}.
{{zpa-deletes}} Directory synchronization behaves differently again: users removed from the directory are deactivated and have their cookies invalidated, see [[zia.ad-integration.directory-sync]].
Whether a live session survives a disable is open {{gap:session-kill}}, and whether tokens or SAML sessions already issued are revoked is open {{gap:token-revocation}}.
The verbs and endpoints are in [[zia.scim.operations]]; how soon the IdP's change arrives at all is in [[zia.scim.propagation]].

checks.do: Whether the IdP sent active=false or a DELETE for the user.
For urgent revocation, use the session and token controls rather than SCIM alone, and do not describe a SCIM disable as an immediate access kill.

active-flag.statement: When active=false is sent for a user, Zscaler disables the user; when active=true, Zscaler enables the user.

quotes: When "active=false," Zscaler disables this user When "active=true," Zscaler enables this user

delete-removes.statement: SCIM is documented for deprovisioning users from the Zscaler database when they are deleted from the user directory, and the Zscaler SCIM servers support Delete User (DELETE /Users/{UserID}); active=false, which disables the user, is a separate path.

quotes: Deprovisioning users from the Zscaler database when users are deleted from your user directory.
Operations Supported by Zscaler SCIM Servers

zpa-deletes.statement: In ZPA, active=false deletes the user, so the same IdP action is reversible in ZIA and destructive in ZPA.

quotes: When "active=false," Zscaler disables this user When "active=true," Zscaler enables this user

idp-deactivation-actions.statement: Okta's Deactivate Users feature deactivates the user in the Zscaler service if the Okta account is deleted or deactivated or has Internet & SaaS unassigned. The PingOne guide lists Delete Users among its supported SCIM features. In the Google Workspace guide's Deprovisioning page the administrator specifies an action and time for when an app is turned off for a user, when a user is suspended from Google and when a user is deleted from Google. The Entra ID mapping sets active from the expression Switch([IsSoftDeleted], , "False", "True", "True", "False").

quotes: Deactivate Users: If a user account is deleted or deactivated in Okta or has Internet & SaaS unassigned, the user is also deactivated in the Zscaler service.
7. On the Deprovisioning page, specify an action and time for:
- When an app is turned off for a user
- When a user is suspended from Google
- When a user is deleted from Google

deletion-request.title: Which SCIM request an IdP sends when a user is deleted from the directory
deletion-request.detail: Per-IdP behavior is now sourced at the feature level (idp-deactivation-actions), but none of the guides shows the request on the wire, so which request each IdP sends for a directory deletion is still open. The page lists deprovisioning users deleted from the directory among SCIM's uses and Delete User (DELETE /Users/{UserID}) among the operations Zscaler's SCIM servers support, and active=false is a separate path that disables the user (delete-removes, active-flag). Whether a directory deletion arrives as that DELETE or as an update setting active=false is not in any captured source, and may differ by IdP. An IdP's SCIM provisioning documentation, or the Zscaler SCIM log for a test deletion, would settle it.
deletion-request.blocks: saying what a directory deletion does to a Zscaler user

session-kill.title: Whether active=false ends a live ZIA session
session-kill.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Whether disabling a user via active=false terminates their active ZIA inspection session, or only blocks future authentication, is not documented; the user cannot authenticate via SAML and policy treats them as inactive, but the current session may persist until it expires. For immediate access revocation do not rely on active=false alone. No captured article states it. A lab test of an active session before and after active=false would settle it.
session-kill.blocks: advice on revoking access for terminated users

token-revocation.title: Whether SCIM disable or delete revokes tokens the user already holds
token-revocation.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Disabling or deleting a ZIA user via SCIM removes access going forward but does not invalidate OAuth tokens or SAML sessions already held; hard revocation requires a ZIdentity token revocation call (the ZIdentity API client reference, a later conversion wave). No captured ZIA article states either half. A lab check and the ZIdentity revocation article would settle it.
token-revocation.blocks: advice on hard revocation after offboarding
